skill.name: happyflow-generator
skill.description: Generates dependency-aware Python happy path tests from OpenAPI and GraphQL specifications, then optionally executes them against target APIs.
skill.summary: Generate ordered Python happy path API tests from OpenAPI and GraphQL specifications.
skill.author: Chaim12345

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms real risks from generated Python execution, full environment inheritance, API credential handling, and outbound requests to user or specification controlled targets. Most Markdown fence detections and endpoint identifier findings are false positives. No prompt injection text was found, but publication should require sandboxing, target confirmation, and secret redaction.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before execution, run in a sandbox, and validate all specification-derived strings before code generation.

remediation.issue: The subprocess receives a copy of the full environment.
remediation.suggestion: Pass a minimal allowlisted environment to subprocess.run and avoid exposing unrelated tokens, keys, or service credentials.

remediation.issue: Credentials can be embedded in generated source and printed in output.
remediation.suggestion: Reference secrets through environment variables or runtime parameters, and redact authorization values from logs and returned scripts.

remediation.issue: Network targets can come from specifications or user input.
remediation.suggestion: Show the spec URL, token URL, base URL, and endpoint list, then require confirmation or an allowlist before requests run.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Execution Of Generated Python
semantic_findings.description: The skill fetches or reads API specifications, interpolates spec-derived paths into Python source, writes the result to a temp file, and executes it. A malicious or malformed specification can influence generated code and network behavior.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow directly connects untrusted specifications to generated source and subprocess execution. The cited lines show parsing, path interpolation, file writing, and execution.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Exposure Through Generated Script Output
semantic_findings.description: User credentials are converted into authorization headers, embedded into generated Python source, and the final script is printed. Secrets can be exposed in transcripts, logs, or copied scripts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code builds headers from tokens, API keys, passwords, and OAuth secrets, serializes AUTH_HEADERS into generated source, then prints the final script.

semantic_findings.title: Spec-Controlled Network Target Receives Credentials
semantic_findings.description: The base URL is taken from the OpenAPI specification and the generated executor applies authentication headers to its session. A hostile specification can direct authenticated requests to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The lines show base_url coming from the specification and auth headers applied to every session request. This is a concrete credential misuse path if a spec is untrusted.

content.value_statement: API teams need fast proof that documented endpoints work together before deeper testing. This skill parses specifications, builds ordered flows, and generates Python scripts that exercise expected successful paths.
actual_capabilities: Parses OpenAPI specifications from URLs or local files and extracts endpoints, schemas, request bodies, and base URLs.
Creates authentication headers for bearer tokens, API keys, Basic auth, and OAuth2 client credentials.
Builds a dependency-aware execution plan from path parameters, HTTP methods, and response schemas.
Generates a Python API flow script with retries, response validation, summaries, and optional parallel execution.
Runs the generated script with retries and returns the final script when requests succeed.
limitations: It can run network requests and generated Python, so users must review targets and credentials first.
GraphQL support is simplified and does not perform full schema introspection.
Generated example values may fail against APIs with complex validation or business rules.
It does not replace dedicated contract testing, security testing, or load testing tools.

use_cases.title: Validate a New API Contract
use_cases.description: Generate a quick happy path script from an OpenAPI document before sharing the API with other teams.

use_cases.title: Prepare Regression Smoke Tests
use_cases.description: Create ordered endpoint checks that confirm core API flows still return successful responses after changes.

use_cases.title: Check Deployment Readiness
use_cases.description: Run a specification-based flow against a staging environment before promoting a release.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Basic Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a public specification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use happyflow-generator with this OpenAPI URL. Generate a sequential happy path test script and summarize the endpoint order before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Use Authentication Safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Authenticated API test with explicit target review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this local OpenAPI file and bearer token. Show the base URL and endpoints first. Wait for confirmation before running requests.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Failed Happy Path Steps
prompt_templates.scenario: Existing generated script has validation or status failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the failed happy path output. Explain the failing step, likely request data issue, and the smallest change needed to retry.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Generated Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before using the script in CI.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate the happy path script, then refactor it to avoid embedded secrets, use environment variables, and add clear target confirmation steps.

output_examples.input: An OpenAPI URL for a simple customer API without authentication.
output: A dependency-ordered endpoint plan for create, read, update, and delete operations.
A generated Python test script description with retry handling and response checks.
A run summary showing total steps, successful requests, failures, and elapsed time.

output_examples.input: A local specification plus a bearer token for a staging API.
output: A target review showing the detected base URL and planned authenticated requests.
A generated happy path flow that uses the provided authorization header.
A recommendation to redact secrets before sharing the generated script.

output_examples.input: A failed generated flow with a validation error on a required field.
output: A concise explanation of the failing step and response status.
A suggested request data adjustment based on the specification schema.
A retry summary after applying the smallest safe change.

best_practices: Review the detected base URL, token URL, and endpoint list before allowing any request execution.
Use staging credentials with limited permissions and redact secrets from generated scripts before sharing.
Run generated scripts in a sandboxed environment with a minimal environment and strict network allowlist.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated scripts against production systems without explicit approval and rate limits.
Do not paste long-lived API keys into prompts or generated source files.
Do not trust specifications from unknown URLs without reviewing server targets and examples first.

faq.question: What specification formats does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports OpenAPI specifications and a simplified GraphQL path. OpenAPI support is more complete.

faq.question: Can it execute requests automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes execution logic, so users should confirm targets and credentials before running it.

faq.question: Does it handle authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It can prepare bearer, API key, Basic, and OAuth2 client credentials headers.

faq.question: Will every generated request pass?
faq.answer: No. Some APIs require business-specific data that cannot be inferred from the specification alone.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production testing?
faq.answer: Use it first in development or staging. Production use needs approval, limits, monitoring, and scoped credentials.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code for specification-based API workflow generation.
